title: [FMLA 09] RCVoltage — RC Series Terminal Voltage of R
summary: Resistor terminal voltage VR in an RC series circuit after a DC voltage V is applied (exponential decay).

body.text: Calculator scroll name: RCVoltage. This is the voltage across the resistor R at time t after DC voltage V is applied to a series RC circuit — not the capacitor charging voltage.
At the instant the switch closes, all of V is across R. Current then dies away as the capacitor fills, so VR falls toward 0. The time unit is RC (resistance × capacitance).

body.caption: Resistor voltage decaying from V. At t = RC, VR has fallen to about 37% of V. Capacitor voltage would be the complementary curve V(1 − e^(−t/RC)).

body.text: Primary inputs: V, R, C, t.

body.title: How to run
items: Press FMLA, then 0, then 9 (or scroll to the name and EXE)

body.label: Units
body.text: Use SI: R in Ω, C in F, t in seconds, V and VR in volts. Official constraints: C, R, t > 0.
